topic: An operation that exceeds the 4
canonical_claim: An operation that exceeds the 4 KiB per-operation cap fails alone, so a pathological head item cannot cause an empty-flush livelock.

topic: On a phased-commit failure, every pool
canonical_claim: On a phased-commit failure, every pool task and outstanding ledger item is drained before rollback; exact rollback uses `dropRefIfMatches` and a preallocated POD outcome slot published immediately after durable promote.

topic: Each worker writes rollback information into
canonical_claim: Each worker writes rollback information into a preallocated, index-addressed per-part slot so a post-promote `bad_alloc` cannot lose a durable ref's outcome.

topic: Worker tasks capture only non-owning transaction
canonical_claim: Worker tasks capture only non-owning transaction references, and rollback or destruction may begin only after an exception-safe join has drained every worker.

topic: Exact rollback records `{ns, ref, manifestid
canonical_claim: Exact rollback records `{ns, ref, manifest_id, created}` inside the serialized `appendRefOps` builder and removes a ref only when `dropRefIfMatches` still sees that exact manifest.

topic: The first worker exception is rethrown
canonical_claim: The first worker exception is rethrown after draining; later worker exceptions are logged and swallowed so they cannot mask the first failure.

topic: The phased cross-part design preserves semantic
canonical_claim: The phased cross-part design preserves semantic equivalence rather than byte identity: folded ref-to-manifest bindings, manifest entries, blob payloads, in-degree, and clean metadata must match, while ref-log packing, IDs, timestamps, and incarnation tags may differ.

topic: A batch failure preserves sequential atomicity
canonical_claim: A batch failure preserves sequential atomicity semantics: earlier members may remain committed, `renameParts` throws before Keeper block-ID registration, and rollback uses exact-manifest matching rather than inventing a new all-or-nothing promise.

topic: The parallel-write implementation plan requires an
canonical_claim: The parallel-write implementation plan requires an exception-safe drain before rollback: all task handles, outcome slots, and exception slots are preallocated, and the drain waits without calling throwing `get()`.

topic: `PartWriteTxn::mergeBlobUploadResults` must prevalidate all results and
canonical_claim: `PartWriteTxn::mergeBlobUploadResults` must prevalidate all results and apply them with build-and-swap or equivalent no-throw replacement so a merge failure leaves the transaction build completely untouched.

topic: If any blob-upload task fails, the
canonical_claim: If any blob-upload task fails, the join drains every task and merges no result; publish fails, the precommit is abandoned, staging cleanup follows the existing policy, and successful sibling bodies remain ordinary GC-reclaimable zero-edge debris.

topic: Upload tasks must capture owning or
canonical_claim: Upload tasks must capture owning or value state, and the callback runner must be scoped so its destructor drains tasks before captured storage is destroyed, including when dispatch throws.

topic: If chunk N fails after earlier
canonical_claim: If chunk N fails after earlier chunks committed, chunks before N remain successful and only chunk N plus the unattempted remainder fail; after any committed chunk, later exceptions are contained within the tenure and a leader whose item already succeeded returns that committed result.

topic: A vanished selected ref-log object causes
canonical_claim: A vanished selected ref-log object causes candidate discard and a bounded fresh LIST restart, whereas decode or apply corruption discards the candidate and propagates immediately without re-listing.

topic: `DENYALLOCATIONSINSCOPE` covers only the pre-existing candidate
canonical_claim: `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` covers only the pre-existing candidate move and atomic tail-counter bumps; candidate construction, logging, events, survivor completion, exception creation, notification, and `materializeCommitted` remain outside the deny region.

topic: A gate-1 `yes` proves the exact
canonical_claim: A gate-1 `yes` proves the exact transferred manifest was the committed binding at confirmation, no removal was durable or in flight past admission, no durable-but-unapplied transaction existed, and the responder was the live writer; any removal appended afterward is ordered after confirmation.

topic: `CasEventDispatcher::emit` serializes concurrent delivery, invokes the
canonical_claim: `CasEventDispatcher::emit` serializes concurrent delivery, invokes the sink outside its mutex, and queues reentrant emissions for the already-running drain loop instead of recursively acquiring the delivery lock.

topic: `uploadPendingBlobs` uses `ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal` inside the scope
canonical_claim: `uploadPendingBlobs` uses `ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal` inside the scope owning captured storage, propagates the query `ThreadGroup`, always drains tasks including dispatch throws, and performs no partial merge on failure.

topic: The TLA+ gate adds the authoritative
canonical_claim: The TLA+ gate adds the authoritative epoch-presence guard, decommission terminal-mount policy, and negative controls showing that removing the guard or blindly minting epoch 1 over a live mount reaches a same-pair two-writer state.

topic: The `PostDurableInstall` `CarvePhaseForTest` hook fires after
canonical_claim: The `PostDurableInstall` `CarvePhaseForTest` hook fires after `putIfAbsentControlled` returns `Committed` and before the candidate is installed, providing the test seam for post-durable failure injection.

topic: `RefApplyState` has `Clean`, `ApplyPending`, and `Poisoned`
canonical_claim: `RefApplyState` has `Clean`, `ApplyPending`, and `Poisoned` states; a successful commit, conclusive PUT failure, definite failure, or absent wedge resolution clears `ApplyPending`, while a post-durable install failure transitions to `Poisoned`, which later successful flushes must never clear. Additionally, `Poisoned` is distinct from wedge: it means a durable transaction may be missing from the cached view, so it blocks snapshot publication and triggers re-recovery. Additionally, A `Poisoned` marker is not sufficient protection before the no-throw install fix: without that fix, later transactions could still publish a snapshot hiding a durable missing transaction, so poison must either follow A1 or become a hard per-namespace fence.

topic: A `Yes` from `confirmExactRef` excludes stale-cache
canonical_claim: A `Yes` from `confirmExactRef` excludes stale-cache, pending, in-flight, wedge, poison, and fence ambiguity but does not prove that the recovered runtime replayed every durable journal record.

topic: The confirm fence rule is evaluated
canonical_claim: The confirm fence rule is evaluated last, so gate-0 `No`, gate-1 `No`, and every `Unknown` reach the same caller outcome; future code must not treat `No` as authoritative without hoisting the fence rule.

topic: The stage-1 composition review found no
canonical_claim: The stage-1 composition review found no Pool/ledger/dispatcher/semaphore lock cycle; the dispatcher releases its mutex before invoking the sink, and condemned-local admission ends before event and metadata work.

topic: A committed transaction that produced blob
canonical_claim: A committed transaction that produced blob deltas but whose deltas reached no shard reducer causes the GC round to throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` before the seal write, adopt nothing, reclaim nothing, and direct recovery through `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD`.

topic: The CAS ref-chain design makes absence
canonical_claim: The CAS ref-chain design makes absence decidable through per-namespace contiguous ids, point reads, conditional writes, and an exact committed-through frontier; a pool-wide allocator that creates per-namespace gaps makes absence undecidable without a certificate.

topic: A missing intermediate epoch or a
canonical_claim: A missing intermediate epoch or a checkpoint frontier after an `EpochSeal` in the same numeric epoch is `CORRUPTED_DATA`; consumers must not shortcut a fold, recovery, `fsck`, or orphan sweep around it.

topic: A checkpoint snapshot may never name
canonical_claim: A checkpoint snapshot may never name an `EpochSeal`; before accepting a nonempty `checkpoint_snapshot_id`, every reader exact-reads the matching `_log` and rejects an `EpochSeal` before reading the same-id `_snap`.

topic: An opaque life id with no
canonical_claim: An opaque life id with no catalog entry is inert debris and never evidence of damage; the only exported catalog deletion transitions are exact-CAS cancellation of a complete terminal `Creating` row and exact-CAS deletion of a complete, unheld `Removing` row with cleanup evidence.

topic: A writer-mount recovery that may have
canonical_claim: A writer-mount recovery that may have landed beyond the durable frontier exact-reads one deterministic successor; matching valid bytes permit the fenced checkpoint contribution, different bytes or an invalid successor are corruption, and absence permits the conditional retry.
